Formatting function for percentage values

Source: R/jjcsformats.R
jjcsformat_fraction.Rd

Formats fractional values as percentages with special consideration for values that round to 0 or 100, as well as missing values. The input is expected to be a fraction, which is multiplied by 100 internally before formatting. Missing values are formatted as "-".

Usage

jjcsformat_fraction(
  x,
  round_type = valid_round_type,
  output = c("ascii", "html"),
  d = 1,
  add_pct = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

(numeric(1))
Fraction to format as a percentage (e.g. 0.15 represents 15%. NA is formatted as "-".

round_type

(character(1))
The type of rounding to perform. See formatters::format_value() for more details.

output

(character(1))
Output type. See formatters::format_value() for more details.

d

(numeric(1))
Number of digits to round the percentage to.

add_pct

(logical(1))
Whether to append the percentage symbol ("%") to the formatted value.

verbose

(logical(1))
Whether to print verbose output.

...

Additional arguments passed to other methods.

Value

A formatted string.

See also

Other JJCS formatting functions: count and fraction related formatting functions, jjcsformat_xx()

Author

WW

Examples

jjcsformat_fraction(0.15)
#> [1] "15.0"
jjcsformat_fraction(0.15, d = 2)
#> [1] "15.00"
jjcsformat_fraction(0.15, d = 2, verbose = TRUE)
#> round_type used: iec
#> [1] "15.00"
